45	CASE OD2-DEV2-CONTRA: Night premium shortfalls after the Fenmarch Water payroll cutover
46	
47	Setting: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
48	
49	Presenting request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. 51	INITIAL EVIDENCE
52	E1 [stage S1] Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
53	E2 [stage S1] Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
54	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
55	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
56	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
57	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
58	E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
59	E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
60	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
61	E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.

65	X2 [stage S1] Ardentra data quality audit: field-level detail of 212 flagged employee records - source: Ardentra data quality team, 6 Nov (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X2.txt

69	X6 [stage S1] October pension contribution file submitted 5 November - source: Fenmarch payroll, pension scheme submission (financial-record) - file: evidence/X6.txt
70	X7 [stage S1] Timesheet portal approval timestamps, October pay period - source: PayLattice timesheet module report, run by Fenmarch payroll, 13 Nov (system-record) - file: evidence/X7.txt
71	X8 [stage S1] IT service desk incident log, cutover weekend 24–26 October - source: Fenmarch IT service desk (log) - file: evidence/X8.txt
72	X9 [stage S1] Contract schedule 7: clause 14.3 and remediation cost provisions - source: Fenmarch procurement, Ardentra master services agreement (document) - file: evidence/X9.txt
73	X10 [stage S1] Operations overtime cover dashboard, September–November - source: Operations performance team (telemetry) - file: evidence/X10.txt
74	X11 [stage S1] Bank payment file and settlement reconciliation, 30 October payment - source: Fenmarch Finance treasury team, 3 Nov (financial-record) - file: evidence/X11.txt
75	X12 [stage S1] Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff - source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document) - file: evidence/X12.txt
76	X13 [stage S1] Programme plan revision history and go-live readiness checklist - source: Programme management office (document) - file: evidence/X13.txt
77	X14 [stage S1] Change advisory board minutes, 21 October - source: Programme CAB secretary (document) - file: evidence/X14.txt
78	X15 [stage S1] Collective agreement extract (night working), legacy night premium rule specification, and functional design FD-07 - source: Fenmarch HR policy library and programme document store (document) - file: evidence/X15.txt
79	X16 [stage S1] PayLattice platform configuration audit trail export, tenant FEN-PRD, 1–31 October - source: Platform audit trail, exported 13 Nov by T. Wierzba (Fenmarch system administrator) (log) - file: evidence/X16.txt

82	H1: The October pay errors stem from inaccurate employee records carried over from the legacy system in the data migration.
83	H2: The October pay errors stem from how pay calculation rules are configured in the new payroll system.
84	H3: The October pay errors stem from hours or shift times recorded incorrectly in the new timesheet portal.
85	H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
86	H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.

90	R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
91	R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)

95	A1: Accept Ardentra's attribution: suspend the HR data team's edit rights pending a conduct review, re-cleanse and reload the full employee master data before the 24 Nov calculation, and absorb the remediation cost under clause 14.3.

98	A4: Roll back PayLattice platform release 7.4 in the production tenant before the November pay run.

101	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
102	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
103	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
104	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
105	S5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
106	S6: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
107	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
108	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
109	S9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
110	S10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
111	S11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
112	S12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
113	S13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
114	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

1	X12 [stage S1]
2	Title: Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff
3	Source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document)
4	
5	Scope: all 158 staff with night hours in October, not only those who raised tickets. Timesheet hours agreed to the rostering system for 158 of 158. Expected premium follows the collective agreement: time-and-a-third for hours worked 20:00–06:00. Result: 147 underpaid, 11 paid correctly. For each of the 147, the shortfall equals 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, to within £0.01. 8 of the 147 had raised no ticket. The 11 paid correctly are Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00. Ardentra flagged list: 19 of 22 flagged night workers were underpaid (86%), against 128 of 136 unflagged (94%). The 190 flagged day workers were paid correctly. Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant (release 7.4, copy of production data) with NSP-02 window_start set to 20:00: all 158 matched expected pay.

input.brief:
The October night premium errors were not caused by Fenmarch's data. They came from one change to the night premium rule (NSP-02) on 22 Oct. It was logged as a label correction, but Ardentra applied a template that also moved the premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform audit trail can't be edited, and it shows this. An internal audit recalculation found 147 of 158 night workers underpaid. Each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 staff paid correctly work 22:00–06:00. Re-running October in the test tenant with 20:00 restored matched expected pay for all 158. The load history shows the production load used the same data as the parallel run, not the later extract Ardentra cited. Flagged records were no more likely to be underpaid than unflagged ones.

What to do: don't suspend the HR team or accept clause 14.3 costs. Don't reload the data. Don't roll back release 7.4. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start, verify it in test, and make off-cycle payments to all 147 before 24 Nov. Review how Ardentra's change log was written and approved. Treat the overtime drop as unproven, because the rota trial started at the same time. Confidence is high.
